issues.description: Constructor parameter order for RollerCoaster is inconsistent with the problem specification (UML + constructor-order rule). The problem statement requires that subclass constructors first accept the attributes of the superclass (in their respective order) followed by the subclass attributes (i.e., RollerCoaster's constructor should accept name, abbreviation, numberOfLoopings). In the solution, RollerCoaster defines its constructor as RollerCoaster(String name, int numberOfLoopings, char abbreviation) (swapping the order), and LaunchedRollerCoaster calls super(...) using a different ordering (super(name, abbreviation, numberOfLoopings)). This mismatch contradicts the explicit constructor-order requirement and will confuse students implementing constructors and may cause compilation/type problems when subclasses attempt to call super(...).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the RollerCoaster constructor follow the UML / problem-rule ordering: accept superclass attributes first in their order, then subclass attributes. For example: public RollerCoaster(String name, char abbreviation, int numberOfLoopings) { super(name, abbreviation); this.numberOfLoopings = numberOfLoopings; }. Then update subclasses (e.g., LaunchedRollerCoaster) to call super(name, abbreviation, numberOfLoopings). Alternatively, if the solution intent was different, update the problem statement UML and the constructor-order requirement to reflect the implemented parameter order — but keeping the problem statement consistent with the template/solution is required.
